options.name: api_auth_cookie
options.description: Authentication cookie for the Checkmk session.

options.name: api_secret
options.description: The secret to authenticate your automation user. If not set the module will fall back to the environment variable C(CHECKMK_VAR_API_SECRET).

options.name: api_user
options.description: The automation user you want to use. It has to be an 'Automation' user, not a normal one. If not set the module will fall back to the environment variable C(CHECKMK_VAR_API_USER).

options.name: client_cert
options.description: Path to the client certificate file for authentication with the web server hosting Checkmk. This is not a Checkmk feature, but one of Ansible and the respective web server.

options.name: client_key
options.description: Path to the client certificate key file for authentication with the web server hosting Checkmk. This is not a Checkmk feature, but one of Ansible and the respective web server.

options.name: comment
options.description: Remarks for the downtime. If omitted in combination with state = present, the default 'Set by Ansible' will be used, in combination with state = absent, ALL downtimes of a host or host/service will be removed.

options.name: duration
options.description: Duration in minutes. When set, the downtime does not begin automatically at a nominated time, but when a non-OK status actually appears for the host. Consequently, the start_time and end_time is only the time window in which the scheduled downtime can occur.

options.name: end_after
options.description: The timedelta between I(start_time) and I(end_time). If you want to use I(end_after) you have to omit I(end_time). For keys and values see U(https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta)

options.name: end_time
options.description: The end datetime of the downtime. The format has to conform to the ISO 8601 profile I(e.g. 2017-07-21T17:32:28Z). The built-in default is 30 minutes after now.

options.name: force
options.description: Force the creation of a downtime in case a hostname and comment combination already exists as a downtime.

options.name: host_name
options.description: The host to schedule the downtime on.

options.name: server_url
options.description: The base url of your Checkmk server including the protocol but excluding the site. If not set the module will fall back to the environment variable C(CHECKMK_VAR_SERVER_URL).

options.name: service_descriptions
options.description: Array of service descriptions. If set only service-downtimes will be set. If omitted a host downtime will be set.

options.name: site
options.description: The site you want to connect to. This will be appended to the server_url as part of the API request url. If not set the module will fall back to the environment variable C(CHECKMK_VAR_SITE).

options.name: start_after
options.description: The timedelta between now and I(start_time). If you want to use I(start_after) you have to omit I(start_time). For keys and values see U(https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta)

options.name: start_time
options.description: The start datetime of the downtime. The format has to conform to the ISO 8601 profile I(e.g. 2017-07-21T17:32:28Z). The built-in default is now.

options.name: state
options.description: The state of this downtime. If absent, all matching host/service-downtimes of the given host will be deleted.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate the SSL certificate of the Checkmk server. If not set the module will fall back to the environment variable C(CHECKMK_VAR_VALIDATE_CERTS).
